english: Let $P_{1}$ be the parabola $y^{2}=4(x+1)$. Let $P_{2}$ be the parabola that has the same focus and the same axis as $P_{1}$ and opens in the opposite direction. If the length of the common chord of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ is $6$, then the distance between the vertices of $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $P_{1}$ परवलय $y^{2}=4(x+1)$ है। माना कि $P_{2}$ वह परवलय है जिसकी नाभि तथा अक्ष $P_{1}$ के समान हैं तथा जो विपरीत दिशा में खुलता है। यदि $P_{1}$ तथा $P_{2}$ की उभयनिष्ठ जीवा की लम्बाई $6$ है, तो $P_{1}$ तथा $P_{2}$ के शीर्षों के बीच की दूरी ______ है।
solution: $P_{2}$ opens towards $-x$ with focus $(0,0)$: vertex $(b,0)$, $b>0$, so $P_{2}:y^{2}=-4b(x-b)$
Then $y^{2}=4b$, so the chord length is $4\sqrt b=6\Rightarrow b=\dfrac94$
solution_full: $y^{2}=4(x+1)$ is $Y^{2}=4X$ with $X=x+1$, so $a=1$, the vertex is $(-1,0)$, the focus is $(-1+1,0)=(0,0)$ and the axis is the $x$-axis.

$P_{2}$ has focus $(0,0)$, axis the $x$-axis, and opens towards the negative $x$-direction, so its vertex is at $(b,0)$ with $b>0$ (the focus lies inside, on the side towards which it opens), and its equation is $y^{2}=-4b(x-b)$.
Points common to both satisfy $4(x+1)=-4b(x-b)$, i.e. $x+1=-bx+b^{2}$, $(1+b)x=b^{2}-1$, so $x=b-1$. Hence the common chord is the line $x=b-1$.
On this line $y^{2}=4(b-1+1)=4b$, so the end points are $(b-1,\pm2\sqrt b)$ and the length is $4\sqrt b$.
The vertices are $(-1,0)$ and $\left(\dfrac94,0\right)$, so the distance between them is $\dfrac94+1=\dfrac{13}{4}=3.25$.
originality_note: New: two coaxial parabolas with a common focus opening in opposite directions; the common chord found by subtracting the equations is x = b - a and has length 4 sqrt(ab), which fixes the second parabola (way 5, the link between the shared focus and the chord). Closest known: confocal parabolas cut orthogonally; common chord of y^2 = 4ax and x^2 = 4by. Different because: the chord length is the data and the unknown parabola is recovered from it.
key_step: Write P2 as y^2 = -4b(x - b) from the shared focus, subtract to get the chord x = b - 1, and use its length 4 sqrt b.
justification: Routine three-step chain: focus of a shifted parabola, family with the same focus, common chord by subtraction. No insight beyond the set-up. Like 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).
stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that 'same focus, same axis, opposite direction' fixes P2 up to one parameter, that P1 and P2 do meet (for every b > 0), and that the common chord is unique. Answer 3.25, a positive decimal. No change.

concept_use.Common chord and common normal of two co: Subtracting the equations of P1 and P2 gives their common chord x = b - 1, whose length 4 sqrt b fixes P2.
